clue.text: A very light-weight magician?

parts.note: a conjuror weighing almost nothing, read as a sorcerer named after the ounce, the tiny unit of weight written oz

explanation.surface: A question about a conjuror who weighs next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: OZ is the abbreviation for an ounce, a very light weight, so the famous humbug sorcerer of the Frank Baum story can be read as a magician weighing an ounce.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Baum's children's novel is a pretend magician ruling the Emerald City.

clue.text: Are there seers more elevated than 'e, say you?

definitions.text: Are there seers more elevated than 'e, say you?

parts.words: Are there seers more elevated than 'e, say you?
parts.note: a dropped-aitch question 'Is 'e 'igher?' about a prophet, which spoken quickly runs together into the name of a major Hebrew prophet

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether any prophet ranks higher than a particular one.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'e drops its H in Cockney style, inviting 'Is 'e 'igher?', which said together sounds like the prophet's name; 'say you?' asks the solver to say it.
explanation.definitionFit: He is one of the major prophets of the Old Testament, a seer of the first rank.

clue.text: A firm's taken on new-style clerical assistants

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: new here tells us the letters of the word style are given a fresh order

explanation.surface: A company has hired some newly fashionable church helpers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new-style' looks like one adjective, but 'new' is the anagram signal on 'style', giving LYTES after A and CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Acolytes are lay helpers who assist priests at the altar, carrying candles and serving at Mass.

clue.text: If it takes another beating, so will the Spaniards

definitions.text: If it takes another beating, so will the Spaniards

parts.words: If it takes another beating, so will the Spaniards
parts.note: refers to the legend that beating a certain Elizabethan admiral's instrument summons him back to defeat England's enemies, as he beat the Armada

explanation.surface: A warning that if something is struck again, Spain will be struck too.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says the drum of Sir Francis Drake, who fought the Spanish Armada, will bring him back to save England when beaten, so the Spaniards would take another beating.
explanation.definitionFit: This snare drum, kept at Buckland Abbey in Devon, is the subject of a famous legend and Newbolt poem.

clue.text: Give prominence to an exploit on the river

parts.note: an exploit is a deed or feat
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, often used in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone is told to highlight a daring deed done on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' places FEAT above the URE.
explanation.definitionFit: To feature something is to highlight it or make it a main attraction.

clue.text: A quarter of an hour playing roulette

definitions.text: A quarter of an hour playing roulette

parts.words: A quarter of an hour playing roulette
parts.note: one letter of the four in the word hour is a round O, which on a roulette layout is the green number that wins for the house

explanation.surface: Someone spends fifteen minutes at the roulette table.
explanation.walkthrough: The time span is a trick: a quarter of the word 'hour' is one of its four letters, and its O looks like a nought, the number on a roulette wheel that favours the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Nought, the house's slot on a roulette wheel, looks like the letter O found in the word hour.

clue.text: Herb drinks a half-bottle-it could damage his works

indicators.note: drinks means the herb takes the other letters inside it, as one swallows a drink

parts.note: sage is a kitchen herb

indicators.note: half of the six-letter word bottle is its first three letters

explanation.surface: A man called Herb has a small bottle of wine and does damage at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Herb reads as a man's name, but it is the plant SAGE, which 'drinks' A plus BOT, the first half of 'bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage is deliberate destruction of plant or machinery, the kind that wrecks a factory.

clue.text: In Peter men see outstanding possibilities

indicators.note: possibilities suggests the letters of these three words can be arranged in other ways

explanation.surface: In Peter, men see great potential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a link; the ten letters of IN PETER MEN rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pre-eminent stands above all others, excelling in their field.

clue.text: Cake transformed Alice, beginning to run

indicators.note: transformed tells us that the name Alice is changed into another order
beginning to points to the first letter of the word run

explanation.surface: A cake changed Alice, which starts her running.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Alice shrinking and growing after eating cake in Wonderland. ALICE rearranged gives ECLAI, then R.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a long choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: It's on the box or in the hat

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a Panama is a straw hat

explanation.surface: Something is either on the box or in the hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the box' is British slang for television; Panorama is a long-running BBC current-affairs programme. OR goes in PANAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Panorama is a BBC current-affairs TV programme, so it is broadcast on television.

clue.text: One of those sliding to the front of the big parade

definitions.text: One of those sliding to the front of the big parade

parts.words: One of those sliding to the front of the big parade
parts.note: a marching band brass instrument whose slide pushes forward, and which traditionally marches in the front rank

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks forward to lead a big procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sliding' suggests a person edging forward; it is the instrument's slide, and trombones march at the front of a band so their slides have room.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a brass instrument played with a moving slide, a staple of marching bands.

clue.text: Talk of a bird or a foreign bird-stalker

definitions.meaning: a small songbird such as the stonechat or whinchat
the French word for cat, a hunter of birds

explanation.surface: Someone talks about a bird or about a cat abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions; 'foreign' points to French, where the word means cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Natter is a chat; stonechats are chats; French for cat is chat, and cats stalk birds.

clue.text: A take-off of a take-off as newspaper 5?

parts.note: a comic is a comedian who does take-offs, or impersonations
to strip is to take off clothes

explanation.surface: A parody of a parody appears as a newspaper item.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 refers to 5-down, FEATURE: a newspaper feature. 'take-off' means a parody the first time and an undressing the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip cartoon is a regular feature in many newspapers.

clue.text: Design for a cigar shop — late entries accepted here

indicators.note: design for suggests the letters are laid out anew to make something

explanation.surface: Plans for a tobacconist that still takes late customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead: stone coffins accept the deceased. The ten letters of A CIGAR SHOP rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: These are stone coffins, into which the dead were placed.

clue.text: Faint trail following 6 of varying hues

indicators.note: following places the faint trail after the piece from 6

parts.note: 6-down is the number zero, written as the letter O
faint means pale
a scent is a trail followed by hounds

explanation.surface: A faint track comes after a nought, in shimmering colours.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 6 is 6-down, ZERO, giving O; PALE SCENT follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Opalescent things show shifting milky colours like an opal.

clue.text: Bill's dance on tape

definitions.meaning: a parliamentary bill or proposed law
an old word for a stately dance
to find dimensions using a tape

explanation.surface: Bill does a dance on tape.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions; the dance sense is archaic, as in 'tread a measure'.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary act is a measure; a stately dance was one; and a tape gauges length.

clue.text: Player captain describes as of lowest degree

annotationWithheld.why: Player captain describes 6 as of lowest degree (8): ABSOLUTE (absolute zero describes 6, ZERO, as lowest) but no reading of 'Player captain' gives ABSOLUTE or its pieces
annotationWithheld.clue: Player captain describes as of lowest degree

clue.text: Peeping Tom's sine qua non in a way ?

definitions.text: Peeping Tom's sine qua non in a way ?

parts.words: Peeping Tom's sine qua non in a way ?
parts.note: a tomcat peeping needs its eye, and the road reflector set in a way is named after that feline eye

explanation.surface: What a voyeur cannot do without.
explanation.walkthrough: A Peeping Tom is a voyeur, but here the Tom is a tomcat; 'way' is a road, where reflective studs bear that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflective road studs marking lanes are named for the glint of a feline eye.

clue.text: One of those American terms see the difference ?

indicators.note: the difference asks for the letters of the two words to be made into something different

explanation.surface: A term in American colleges, asking whether you see how it differs.
explanation.walkthrough: TERMS and SEE rearranged make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-year academic periods are standard in American colleges in place of the British three-term year.

clue.text: Mr Pott edited this Eatanswill paper

definitions.text: Mr Pott edited this Eatanswill paper

parts.words: Mr Pott edited this Eatanswill paper
parts.note: in Dickens's Pickwick Papers the editor Pott runs a newspaper in the town of Eatanswill

explanation.surface: A literary question about a newspaper editor in a Dickens town.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Pickwick Papers, Mr Pott edits the Eatanswill Gazette, rival of the Independent.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazette is a newspaper, the title of Pott's paper in Pickwick.

clue.text: Such things specially ordered for use by Abigail, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: an Abigail is an old word for a lady's maid, so her things are a maid's costume

explanation.surface: Bespoke items ordered for a woman called Abigail.
explanation.walkthrough: An Abigail is a lady's maid (from a servant in Beaumont and Fletcher); clothing for her is a 'costume maid', which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bespoke goods are made to a buyer's order rather than off the shelf.

clue.text: Many paintings etc on sale here

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, many
paintings and the like are art

explanation.surface: Lots of artworks are being sold in a place.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a market, a place where goods are on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A mart is a market or trading place, where goods are sold.

clue.text: One of the fools, say, dashing into the country

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, giving a similar sound

parts.note: from 'fools rush in where angels fear to tread', a fool is one who rushes in

explanation.surface: A foolish person runs headlong into a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dashing into' completes the picture of 'fools rush in'; a rusher, said in British speech without the final R, sounds like the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia is the largest country in the world, spanning Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Revealing the story of William

parts.note: William Tell is the Swiss archer of legend
a story is a tale

explanation.surface: The tale of William is told.
explanation.walkthrough: William Tell shot an apple from his son's head; his story is a TELL TALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale sign gives something away, betraying a secret.

clue.text: Olympian 15s

definitions.meaning: a god living on Mount Olympus, the Greek god of war
15-across is MEASURE; these are metric units of area, each a hundred square metres

explanation.surface: Olympian measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 15s points to 15-across: these are measures of land area in the metric system.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek war god dwells on Olympus, and the metric unit of a hundred square metres is a unit of area.

clue.text: Sound agreements to work on the subject

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is identified by how it is heard

parts.note: agreements between nations are treaties

explanation.surface: Solid agreements to work on a matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid; it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written study of a subject.

clue.text: Deceive, with transposition, the new recruits

indicators.note: with transposition says the two parts of the phrase swap places

parts.note: to deceive someone is to take them in

explanation.surface: Fooling the new recruits by switching things round.
explanation.walkthrough: TAKE IN with its parts swapped gives IN TAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: An intake is the batch of new entrants admitted at one time.

clue.text: Dish which Alaska's old-timer never made

definitions.text: Dish which Alaska's old-timer never made

parts.words: Dish which Alaska's old-timer never made
parts.note: an Alaskan prospector is nicknamed a sourdough after his bread, so he would never make the opposite kind

explanation.surface: A dish no veteran Alaskan ever cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Old-timers in Alaska and the Yukon are called sourdoughs; the pun is that a sourdough would never make bread that is the opposite, though the answer is really offal, the pancreas or thymus.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetbreads are a dish of calf or lamb glands, usually thymus or pancreas.
